I have $546 and am on INDIANA_AVENUE. My light blue set has 4/3/3 houses. I can build to 4 on Vermont and Connecticut.

The bank has 4 houses and 12 hotels remaining.

Claude (p1) is on B&O Railroad with $63. He owns Kentucky and Illinois unmortgaged, but Indiana is mortgaged so he cannot build on the red set.

Standard Monopoly rent values are now clear. p2's orange set pays $750–$1000 per house. His dark blue properties pay $1100–$2000 per house. My light blues pay $270–$400 per house. Landing on his dark blue properties would be catastrophic.

Building both light blue properties to four houses costs $100 and would raise my rent income to $400–$450. I am weighing whether that investment is worthwhile. I am also checking the board order to see which players can land on my light blues before I benefit.

I mapped the full board order. From Ventnor Avenue, p2 can reach Water Works in one space and Boardwalk in twelve. The light blue properties sit between Indiana Avenue and Boardwalk.

p2 cannot reach my light blue properties this turn. From Ventnor, the maximum move of 12 spaces lands on Boardwalk, not the light blues.

p1 also cannot reach them this turn. From B&O Railroad, the furthest he can go is Park Place.

The turn order is p4, p1, p2. Neither opponent can reach my light blue properties before my next roll. Building houses now would not generate rent until after they move again.

I am now considering the sequence after my turn ends. p1 and p2 cannot reach my light blue properties this turn, so I would roll from Indiana next. I am checking whether a mortgaged property in a color group blocks double rent on the other properties in that set.

I am uncertain about the official rule on mortgaged properties in a color group. I am also dismissing the threat from Illinois, since it is unmortgaged but has zero houses and would only cost $20 or $40. From Indiana Avenue, the next spaces are B&O Railroad and Atlantic Avenue, both owned by p2 and mortgaged.

From Indiana Avenue, the next spaces are Water Works, Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, Pacific Avenue, North Carolina Avenue, Community Chest, Pennsylvania Avenue, and Short Line. The orange properties sit behind me on the board, so I would not land on them from here. The dark blue properties are still several spaces away.

The minimum roll from Indiana to Park Place is fourteen spaces, so I cannot reach it or Boardwalk this turn. The orange properties are also behind me. My next roll will be relatively safe. After that I will move ahead two to twelve spaces, and p1 and p2 will still not be near my light blue properties unless they go around the board.

I am now calculating the liquidity impact of building houses. I have $546 in cash. I can mortgage States Avenue for $70 and Ventnor Avenue for $130. Each light blue house costs $50 to build but sells back for only $25. I need to weigh whether the immediate $100 cost is worth the future rent income.

I have ten houses in total, worth $250 if sold. Unmortgaging my mortgaged properties would cost roughly $700 plus interest. Building Vermont and Connecticut to four houses costs $100 and leaves me with $446. That would raise my rent from $270 to $400 on Vermont and from $300 to $450 on Connecticut. The extra income is significant, but I am weighing whether the lower cash balance will hurt me when I eventually land on the orange and dark blue sets.

p2 has $162 in cash. He already owns four houses on all three orange properties. He can now build a hotel on one orange for $100, which returns the four houses to the bank.

p2 can build a hotel on one orange property for $100, since the bank has four houses and twelve hotels available. That would raise orange rent to $950 or $1000. He cannot build a dark blue house yet because he only has $162 and needs $200 per property. Even mortgaging Baltic Avenue would leave him short.

p2 cannot upgrade his dark blue properties this turn. He has only $162 and would need $200 per house, so mortgaging Baltic Avenue still leaves him short by $8.

He can still build a hotel on one orange property for $100, which would raise orange rent to $950 or $1000. That is worse than the current $750 or $800.

Building my own houses cannot prevent p2 from upgrading his properties on his turn.

I am now looking for a trade that could help me. I notice that p1 owns all three red properties: Kentucky, Indiana (mortgaged), and Illinois.

p1 cannot unmortgage Indiana Avenue because it costs $121 and he only has $63. He is effectively broke with no houses and one incomplete monopoly.

p2 remains the dominant threat with his orange and dark blue monopolies.

My win condition is to survive p2's orange and dark blue sets until they land on my light blues and go broke, or to trade for a better position. Four-house light blue rent would not bankrupt p2, who still holds $162.

p2 has roughly $1,200 in building equity plus cash and Baltic Avenue. A single light blue hit would not bankrupt him. Hotel rent on those properties would also be insufficient. He would need multiple hits to go broke.

I calculated my total liquid assets. Without mortgaging light blue deeds, I have roughly $996. If I sell all ten houses and mortgage every light blue property, plus States and Ventnor, my total rises to about $1,156.

Fully liquidating everything would barely cover a three-house Park Place hit, leaving only about fifty-six dollars. Boardwalk at three houses would still leave me short by two hundred forty-four dollars. p2 cannot build a fourth house on Park Place because he lacks the additional eighty dollars needed. This is a survival game.

I should maximize liquidity to survive dark blue hits while keeping the light blue monopoly as a weapon.

Previous thoughts said: don't build because it reduces cushion against orange/dark blue. That logic still holds somewhat.

Current cash $546, non-LB liquidity = $546 + $70 + $130 + $250 = $996.
Park Place 3h = $1100, short $104. I'd need to mortgage a light blue ($50-$60) to survive Park Place, which means selling ALL houses first (even building) because you can't mortgage a property with houses, and you must sell houses evenly...

Mortgaging one light blue property requires selling all houses on the entire monopoly. The $250 house resale is already counted in the $996 base liquidity. Adding one light blue deed mortgage brings the total to roughly $1,046–$1,056, still short of the $1,100 needed for a three-house Park Place hit. Mortgaging two light blue deeds would reach about $1,096, or mortgaging Oriental and Connecticut would reach $1,106. To survive that hit, I would need to mortgage two light blue properties and destroy the monopoly’s building potential. I would keep one light blue unmortgaged.

Boardwalk at three houses is impossible to survive even if every light blue property is mortgaged. Building two more houses would cost $100 but only return $50 in resale value, so net liquidity drops by $50 and makes surviving a Park Place hit harder. Building is negative expected value for survival against the dark blue monopolies.

A roll of seven would land me in Jail. From there, reaching Park Place requires twenty-seven spaces and multiple turns. The immediate danger from the dark blue monopolies is therefore delayed.

The next roll from Indiana is safe. The first dangerous roll will come after p1 and p2 move, so the immediate decision is to end the turn.

I will not build houses now. I will preserve cash and reassess after the safe roll.

I am now evaluating trade options. Breaking p2's orange or dark blue monopolies is unlikely because those sets are his win condition. Giving States Avenue to p2 would complete his pink monopoly, so that is a bad idea. I am considering whether giving him the green properties Pacific Avenue or North Carolina Avenue would help.

Completing the green monopoly would give p2 a third set and is rejected again. I considered trading with p1, but he is weak and not the threat. Keeping him alive as a potential shield against p2 is more useful than buying his red properties.

p1 has already refused to sell red properties. Completing a brown monopoly with Baltic Avenue would yield only modest rent and would waste cash I need for dark blue survival. No useful trades remain, so ending the turn is the best option.

Unmortgaging Reading Railroad would cost $220 for only $50 in rent, so it is a poor use of cash. Unmortgaging Water Works would cost about $82 with almost no rent return. Telegraphing weakness through trades should also be avoided.

Mortgaging States or Ventnor would yield cash but sacrifice rent collection, and I have enough liquidity to wait. Selling houses would weaken my position, so I will not do that either.

I will end the turn. I will send a brief strategic message to p1, warning him not to sell p2 red properties and reinforcing our alliance against p2. I will avoid revealing my cash reserves or my fear of Boardwalk. I am also checking whether any building option could be positive.

I can build houses on Vermont and Connecticut, but not hotels yet because Oriental Avenue already has four houses while the others have three. I would need to build both properties to four houses first, which costs $100, before I could even consider a hotel.

I will end the turn. I plan to message p1: "Holding. If you hit orange, sell houses not deeds — don't hand p2 a red." From B&O, p1's next rolls mostly land on mortgaged properties.

A roll of twelve from B&O would land p1 on Park Place with three houses and bankrupt him. He has only $63 cash and about $293 in mortgageable assets, so the $1,100 rent would wipe him out. That would hand p2 his red properties. This makes it critical to keep p1 alive.
